doc.title: Bobby Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Influences, Adele Girard and the harp record
summary: Gordon cites Pee Wee Russell and Marsala, and loved playing with Adele Girard's jazz harp; a recording from her comeback is played.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Where do you feel you fit in to the sound of your fellow clarinetists. Do you emulate anybody? Were you highly influenced by anybody besides Joe Marsala?

I was highly influenced by Pee Wee Russell quite a bit. I always enjoyed his playing. And the type of playing that I really like to do myself is I used to work with Joe Marsala’s wife, Adele Girard. She was a great jazz harpist. She was the first swing harpist to come along in the 1900s. Casper Reardon and a couple of others came along. But I used to just like to play with her and Joe and play together, two clarinets and jazz © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-
harp, which is very nice, it has a very pretty sound. And that was probably some of the most fun I’ve ever had playing.
Well speaking of that, I wanted to play name that tune with you. Does this tune sound [humms]— you know that tune, right?
Yeah, I think I know it. You mean “Don’t Let it End?”
Yeah. I sang it pretty badly. Actually I have a thing I wanted you to listen to here.
You can hear the harp on there.
Yeah. It must have been a pleasure to make this record.

It was because it’s something I always wanted to do and never had the chance to, and Adele said she’d come out of retirement to do it, so we had a great band in Los Angeles when we did this record. And it got a lot of awards too, a lot of awards.
It’s got a great write-up on it and I like the sound of the harp and the piano in there.
Yes, the mixture is beautiful, yeah. Thank you.
